reason: H0 exclusively configures and exercises JSON decoding, so it cannot reach the CRC64 implementation. S1 materially aggravates that gap by adding a new length-sensitive eight-byte path in ecma_hasher.update!, including seven additional ECMA_TABLE rows, while retaining the one-byte tail path. This is more than the historical absence alone because the commit introduces a substantial new implementation branch that H0 cannot execute or control.
evidence: H0 defines WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__JSON and WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__AUX__JSON, but no CRC64 module.
H0 calls wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson; it never invokes ecma_hasher.update! or ecma_hasher.update_u64!.
S0 ecma_hasher.update! has only iterate length: 1, advance: 1 using ECMA_TABLE[0].
S1 ecma_hasher.update! adds iterate length: 8, advance: 8 with accesses to p[0x00] through p[0x07] and ECMA_TABLE[0x00] through ECMA_TABLE[0x07], plus the original one-byte else path.
ECMA_TABLE expands from roarray[1] roarray[256] base.u64 to roarray[8] roarray[256] base.u64.
recommended_action: Add a CRC64 harness entry point that initializes an ecma_hasher and fuzzes update! or update_u64! with arbitrary bytes and varied chunk boundaries, especially lengths below, equal to, above, and multiples of eight with tails; validate one-shot and incrementally chunked checksums agree.
